decisions.reason: This plugin is adjacent to the firm's pricing and digital information capabilities, so management would likely keep it while learning from early customer use, though it is somewhat more technical than the core business.

An ERP interface plugin lies furthest from a market research and advertising firm's established knowledge base, so absorptive-capacity logic suggests a higher chance of withdrawal if early learning and improvement are harder to achieve.
Price comparison tracking fits closely with the firm's existing strengths in market observation, data interpretation, and commercial analytics, making it a strong candidate to retain and refine.

Because this product builds directly on the firm's related knowledge in tracking competitors and prices, management would likely see good scope to learn from the launch and improve it rather than abandon it.
This plugin remains close to the firm's core analytical capabilities, and even if it overlaps with similar offerings, the shared knowledge base makes continued development more likely than exit.

Net price reporting is well aligned with the firm's reporting and analytical expertise, so management would usually keep it on the market while using initial feedback to strengthen its value proposition.
